_doc: CAL-010 village almanac: one omen per day (Almanac.omen_for), picked by weight from `omens`. Fields: id, name (<= 30 chars), text (a string, or an array of strings picked by day; each <= 120 chars), weight (>= 1), boost {} with optional keys fishing_mult 1.0..1.3, gather_bonus 0..0.25 (chance of one extra herb unit), gift_favor 0..3 (extra favor on a liked/neutral gift), sell_mult 1.0..1.1, practice_mult 1.0..1.25. Empty boost = a plain day. Optional talk: 1-4 strings (each <= 90 chars) that villagers say as greetings 25% of the time on that day (FOLK-033). Never touches qi, breakthroughs or combat.

omens.name: An ordinary day
text: The almanac shrugs. Mend your nets, hoe your rows, and be done by dusk.
The headman checked the stars and found nothing worth saying. Good enough.
Plain day, plain bowl of rice. The old folk call that a blessing.

omens.name: Neither good nor ill
text: Neither the toad nor the crow has an opinion today. Carry on.
The river god is napping. Nothing owed, nothing promised.
An in-between day, the old women say: sweep the step and wait.

omens.name: Good for fishing
text: The water is calm and the fish are hungry.
Still water, low mist: the river god has left the larder open.
Old Gui's knees say the carp are close to the bank today.
talk: Calm water today. Old Gui is already down at the pond.
Fish are hungry, they say. Go and see.

omens.name: Good for gathering
text: Herbs stand thick and bright on the hillsides.
The terraces are green to the ridgeline; bring a bigger basket.
Grandmothers say a leaf picked on a bright day keeps its bite.
talk: The slope is thick with herbs this morning.
Bring a basket today; the hills are generous.

omens.name: Good for gifts
text: Hearts are open today; a gift is warmly received.
A small present on a soft day is worth two at the harvest feast.
The headman says doors open easier when the sparrows sing.
talk: A fine day for kind gestures, don't you think?
Hearts are open today, I feel it.

omens.name: Good for trade
text: Buyers are generous when the wind sits in the east.
East wind, open purses: so the drovers say, and they should know.
The market crows are loud today; coin changes hands with a smile.

omens.name: Good for practice
text: Hands and mind are quick; practice sinks in deeper.
The farm saying goes: a sharp morning, a sharp blade. Go and practise.
Ink flows, breath settles; the old teachers called this a gift day.

omens.name: Fish rise to the bait
text: The river god is in a good mood; the carp are rising to every hook.
Silver backs break the pond since dawn. The river god is laughing.
Pour a cup at the jetty today; the river god is in a giving mood.

omens.name: Heavy morning dew
text: Dew hangs on every leaf; the herb slope smells green and strong.
The mist left its pearls on the terraces. Pick them before noon.
Heavy dew, heavy roots, says the herbwife. Go early.

omens.name: Market-day wind
text: Drovers sing out their prices and nobody haggles hard today.
The bells ring true and the scales hang fair; buy and sell with a light heart.
Even stingy Old Fen is rounding up today, the stall-boys whisper.

omens.name: A day for kind words
text: Even the headman smiles; small gifts are remembered all year.
A kind word today will be repaid before the turn of the year.
Mothers say: give on a gentle day, and the gift grows roots.

omens.name: Steady hands
text: The cicadas are quiet, the lamp burns straight; work goes smooth.
No wind in the paper window. A good day to thread a needle or a technique.
Says the carpenter: a patient heart and a level hand. Begin now.

omens.name: Nets hang heavy
text: Old Gui says the nets will hang heavy by dusk; he is seldom wrong.
The herons are fishing the shallows early; the nets will follow.
Gulls over the pond since dawn. Fetch the big nets, the boys say.
